newsitem.title: USA: US Northeast daily power steady after Monday drop.
newsitem.headline: US Northeast daily power steady after Monday drop.

text.p: Day-ahead electricity prices in the northeastern U.S. Tuesday held steady against Monday's level amid the lackluster heating demand in the region.
"Today and yesterday (prices) were all about the same," said a New York electricity trader.
Forecasts indicated temperatures would rise six to 10 degrees F above normal Wednesday and begin to cool Thursday. Readings were expected to fall back to normal levels Saturday.
Precipitation would move through the region late today with chance of snow in the northern sections.
Peak, non-firm electricity prices (including transmission) for Wednesday in the eastern half of the New York Power Pool (NYPP) held in a $26.00-$30.00 a megawatt hour (MWh) range.
Off-peak, non-firm power for day-ahead delivery in eastern NYPP stayed at $23.00-$24.00.
In western NYPP, peak, non-firm power for Wednesday stablized at $20.00-$24.00 after Monday's drop.
Western NYPP electricity for off-peak, non-firm delivery Wednesday remained at $16.00-$18.00.
Prescheduled sales to the Pennsylvania-New Jersey-Maryland (PJM) Interconnect from western New York slowed considerably due to falling prices in the PJM region, market sources said.
Peak, firm electricity prices for next-day delivery in PJM fell $1.50-$2.00/MWh to the low $20.00 range today.
In the New England Power Pool (NEPOOL), peak, non-firm electricity prices at Northeast Utilities' (NU) border continued to hold at $32.00-$35.00.
Next-day, peak deals for deliveries within NEPOOL were reportedly done in a $34.00-$35.00 range.
Non-firm, off-peak NEPOOL power for next-day delivery at the NU border was still assessed at $25.00-$28.00.

The two units at the Indian Point nuclear complex north of New York City remained shut. The 975 megawatt (MW) unit 2 shut January 18 to correct problems with a feedwater valve. No startup date has been scheduled while the operator Con Edison awaits a meeting with the Nuclear Regulatory Commission (NRC) prior to restart.
The 965 MW Indian Point unit 3 was expected to stay idled through mid-February for replacement work in its primary containment area.

Separately, NRC said Tuesday it could not predict when the 910 MW Maine Yankee nuclear power plant would be able to return to service. The facility was shut in December because of an electrical cable problem.
Swing natural gas values at the New York City gate held at $3.00 per million British thermal unit area, flat from Monday.
